features.name: mean_first_paragraph_words
features.definition: What is the mean number of words in the first paragraph of the counter-argument comments?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments as a JSON list of strings. For each comment, strip leading/trailing whitespace, split on one or more blank lines (regex r'\n\s*\n'), take the first non-empty chunk as the first paragraph, and count words as len(re.findall(r"\b\w+(?:['’-]\w+)*\b", chunk)). Return the mean across comments with non-empty text. Empty list or no non-empty comments -> null; missing or unparseable JSON -> null. Comments with no blank-line break count their whole text as the first paragraph. Raw text, no semantic filtering.

h0: mean_first_paragraph_words has no association with the probability that the OP changed their view (delta).
h1: Lower mean_first_paragraph_words is associated with a higher probability that the OP changed their view.
note: Persuasiveness is operationalized as the dataset outcome delta (OP view change); association only, not causal. Shorter first paragraph is measured as mean word count of first paragraph across all supplied counter-comments, assuming paragraphs are separated by blank lines (newline formatting may be lost in some comments, making the whole comment one paragraph). The hypothesis does not specify aggregation across comments; mean chosen. Comments are unordered; no per-comment outcome, so the mean is a row-level summary. Raw text may include quoted text, edits or outcome announcements; this is not filtered. Comment timing relative to the outcome is unknown.
